sentence: S/2019/171 Report of the Panel of Experts established pursuant to resolution 1874 (2009) Summary 19-01704 The nuclear and ballistic missile programmes of the Democratic People ’s Republic of Korea remain intact and the country continues to defy Security Council resolutions through a massive increase in illegal ship-to-ship transfers of petroleum products and coal.

In its letter to Singapore, the Panel noted the systemic violations of the resolutions taking place at Nampo and also noted that according to a number of the Panel’s previous reports, the port was also the site for the export or import of a variety of shipping containers seized by Member States and found to be containing items from or destined for the Democratic People’s Republic of Korea that violated the provisions of the resolutions, including the measures aimed at stemming nuclear, ballistic missile and other arms-related materials.

The Panel surveyed, confirmed and reported ballistic missile activity sites and found evidence of a consistent trend on the part of the Democratic People’s Republic of Korea to disperse its assembly, storage and testing locations.

According to Global Trade Atlas data, China and Thailand exported a total of $1,867,621 in transportation vehicles (HS codes 86–89) between January and February 2018 to the Democratic People’s Republic of Korea which violated paragraph 7 of resolution 2397 (2017).
